title: Archimedes' principle: the push of a fluid
goal: See how the buoyant force on an object depends on the volume of fluid it displaces.
note: An object in a fluid is pushed upwards by a buoyant force. The force equals the weight of the fluid the object displaces.

graphs.title: The buoyant force rises in a straight line as the volume of water displaced increases.
graphs.label: Buoyant force

sentences: The fluid is water, and its density is 1000 kg/m3.
The buoyant force on the object equals the weight of the water it pushes aside.

predict.prompt: A block pushes aside more water as more of it is pushed under the surface. What happens to the buoyant force on it?
predict.reveal: Increase the volume of water displaced and watch the buoyant force.

concept_check.question: According to Archimedes' principle, the buoyant force on an object in a fluid is equal to what?
options: The weight of the fluid displaced
concept_check.explanation: Archimedes' principle states that the buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid the object displaces.

hints: The fluid pushes up on the object.
What does the buoyant force depend on, the object or the fluid it pushes aside?
The buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid displaced.
